title: Coronavirus NSP14 drives internal m7G modification to rewire host splicing and promote viral replication.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed both processed files in GEO (Gene Expression Omnibus) series GSE307386: GSE307386_AS_events_INPUT_all_samples.tsv.gz (6,200 rows x 18 columns, 364 KB gzipped) and GSE307386_AS_events_IP_all_samples.tsv.gz (8,632 rows x 18 columns, 444 KB gzipped). Confirmed columns (gene symbol, event ID, hg38 coordinates, event length, per-replicate PSI (percent spliced in) for 3 NSP14 and 3 control libraries, dPSI, group, event type, condition means); confirmed minimum absolute dPSI is exactly 15.0 in both files, i.e. only already-changed events are deposited and unchanged events are absent; confirmed no duplicate event IDs; confirmed 2,868 events appear in both files; measured replicate spread (mean standard deviation across the 3 NSP14 replicates 7.4 PSI in poly(A) and 11.5 PSI in m7G-pulldown, versus 1.5 and 2.9 in controls); found that in the IP file 3,116 of 8,632 rows (all non-intron events that go down) carry dPSI as an unsigned magnitude and a sign-flipped 'overlap' column, while the INPUT file is internally consistent; confirmed coordinates are genome build hg38 (TSPAN6 exon at chrX:100,636,191 matches hg38, not hg19).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That libraries were poly(A)-selected or anti-m7G immunoprecipitated RNA from HEK293T cells, that splicing was quantified with VAST-TOOLS v2.5.1 against VastDB hg38 (Hs2), and that events were called differential at absolute dPSI >= 15 with replicate distributions non-overlapping by >= 5 percentage points. Also taken from the text: that an N7-methyltransferase-dead mutant (M4) condition exists; its 6 libraries are listed in GEO but are not present in either processed table. All m7G site locations, western blots, mass-spectrometry nucleoside quantification and virus titres come from figures only, not from any deposited file.

a1_downloadable.note: Both processed tables fetched anonymously from the GEO FTP (file transfer) site and parsed; no login or access application. Verified in the files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: dPSI (splicing change), direction (GROUP = UP/CTRL) and six per-replicate PSI values are literal columns. Caveat: the label for the paper's headline quantity (where internal m7G sits) is in no file, and 'responds vs does not respond' cannot be built because unchanged events were filtered out before deposit.

a3_inputs_present.note: Sequence is not in the file, but exact hg38 coordinates are, and the build is stated, so inputs come from one bulk genome FASTA extraction (~1 GB download), not thousands of per-item lookups. Verified coordinates against hg38.

a4_units_stated.note: Values are percent spliced in, 0-100 (verified range), with the definition in the methods. But the deposit has no README, and in the IP table 3,116 rows store dPSI unsigned, so the sign must be recomputed from the two condition-mean columns.

a5_enough_rows.note: 6,200 poly(A) events over 2,496 genes plus 8,632 m7G-pulldown events over 4,612 genes, counted in the files. All are above the differential threshold; there are zero unchanged events.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~1.2 GB (two sub-MB tables plus one hg38 genome FASTA)
a6_fits_laptop.note: Tables are under 1 MB each; peak memory for the baseline is a couple of GB. Verified by loading both files.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: The files reproduce the paper's stated filter exactly (minimum absolute dPSI 15.00, minimum replicate non-overlap 5.0), so the deposit matches the methods. The paper reports event counts only in bar charts, so no text count could be compared; the short methods paragraph says rMATS while the detailed section and the file contents say VAST-TOOLS.

a8_label_provenance.note: PSI is computed from aligned RNA-sequencing reads by VAST-TOOLS, a quantification tool, not predicted by a model, and it is independent of the genomic-sequence features a model would use. Verified that per-replicate read-derived PSI values are present.

B1.why: Two files, clean per-file event key, but exon events and intron events use different ID namespaces; seen in files.

B2.why: Both gzipped tab-separated files parsed first try with pandas, no fixing needed; done.

B3.why: PSI consistent within a file, but poly(A) and pulldown libraries are not comparable; IP dPSI signs inconsistent.

B4.why: 1,059 of 8,632 IP rows have missing replicate PSI from low coverage; easy to drop; counted in file.

B5.why: Zero duplicate event IDs in either file; the 2,868 shared events are two different assays, not duplicates.

B6.why: No README in the deposit; 'overlap' and 'COMPLEX' columns had to be reverse-engineered; methods document the rest.

C1.why: A null result is ambiguous: could mean sequence does not encode the response, or just 3 noisy replicates.

C2.why: SpliceAI, Pangolin, SpliceAI2, DeltaSplice open and strongly evaluated for splicing; none for NSP14-induced change.

C3.why: Nobody has modelled coronavirus-NSP14-induced splicing, but one cell line and one construct make the angle thin.

C4.why: Labels require transfection, anti-m7G immunoprecipitation and RNA-sequencing; genuinely costly to generate, per methods.

C5.why: Majority-class dummy is 60.1% in the poly(A) table (counted), and SpliceAI/Pangolin give published baselines.

D1.why: Open DNA language models fit this data type: SpliceBERT, DNABERT-2, Nucleotide Transformer, HyenaDNA, all downloadable.

D2.why: 14,832 windows of 1 kb embed once on a laptop CPU in hours; SpliceAI-style 10 kb context would not.

D3.why: Weights are public on Hugging Face; I did not open each licence file, so terms unverified per model.

E1.why: Gene symbol column and chromosome (from coordinates) support held-out-gene and held-out-chromosome splits; both seen in files.

E2.why: 2,496 and 4,612 genes, 24 chromosomes; plenty of groups to hold out; counted in files.

E3.why: Majority class 3,725 of 6,200 (60.1%) and per-event-type rates computable directly from the tables.

E4.why: Three replicates per condition; I measured replicate standard deviation 7.4 PSI (poly(A)) and 11.5 PSI (pulldown).

E5.why: Known intron-retention determinants (short, GC-rich introns, weak donor sites) and event length must be recoverable.

E6.why: Label shuffling within event type and dinucleotide-shuffled sequence windows both trivially runnable on this table.

E7.why: No independent NSP14 splicing dataset; no year or source column; comparable data needs raw-read reprocessing.

E8.why: The paper's dPSI distributions and intron-retention gene list are exactly recomputable from the deposited table.

G1.why: hg38 coordinates, gene symbols, Ensembl gene and transcript IDs for intron events; all present in files.

G2.why: m7GHub V2.0 holds 430,898 m7G sites mapped to hg38, joinable on coordinates; confirmed by its NAR paper.

G3.why: Coordinate-overlap joins are one-to-many (several m7G sites per intron); manageable with a stated collapse rule.

G4.why: Asks whether independently mapped m7G sites sit inside the introns NSP14 retains, testing the paper's mechanism.

H1.why: Verified: minimum absolute dPSI is 15.0, so unchanged events were filtered out before deposit. No negatives.

H2.why: One cell line (HEK293T), one lab, one over-expression construct, three replicates; from GEO sample list.

H3.why: The claim is statable precisely in one sentence; see honest_claim_h3.

H4.why: The paper states the dPSI >= 15 filter, but the GEO files carry no README saying the table is pre-filtered.

I1.why: Coronavirus epitranscriptomics and m7G/METTL1 labs would read it, but no single named group needs it.

I2.why: At best nominates introns for reverse-transcription PCR validation; unlikely to redirect an experimental programme.

I3.why: Precision among a top-50 list matches the validate-by-PCR decision; direction accuracy only roughly matches it.

I4.why: A short, GC-rich, weak-splice-site rule may capture most of the signal; needs the dumb baseline first.

J1.why: Grouped splits, frozen DNA-language-model embeddings, calibration and leakage checks: real modelling practice.

J2.why: Splicing and intron retention are reasonably checkable against literature, but m7G biology is unfamiliar territory.

J3.why: A sign-corrected, documented event table plus the replicate-noise estimate is shareable even if the model fails.

J4.why: No weeks budget written anywhere yet; the small data suggests 2-3 weeks but it is not committed.

J5.why: No kill date in NOTES.md; a condition is proposed in success_criteria but not yet written down.

existing_models.name: SpliceAI (deep network predicting splice sites from DNA sequence, Illumina, 2019)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported 0.95 top-k accuracy on held-out chromosomes for splice-site prediction in its own paper; a 2024 comparison reports Spearman 0.63 for SpliceAI2 versus 0.47 for Pangolin on 4,545 cryptic splice variants (read in search results, not reproduced by me).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Condition- and perturbation-specific splicing (how a given cellular state changes inclusion) is outside what it models; it predicts annotation-like splice-site probability only.

existing_models.name: Pangolin (quantitative splice-site usage from sequence, Genome Biology 2022)
existing_models.score_and_split: Trained on RNA-sequencing splice-site usage across four species with tissue-specific output heads; outperformed SpliceAI on quantitative usage in its own evaluation (from the paper's abstract, not reproduced).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Usage is modelled per tissue from reference sequence; the effect of a specific trans-acting perturbation such as a viral methyltransferase is not addressed.

existing_models.name: DeltaSplice / SpliceAI2 (reference-informed prediction of splicing-altering mutations, 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: SpliceAI2 reported Spearman 0.63 on 4,545 cryptic splice variants versus Pangolin 0.47 (search result summary; I did not open the weights or rerun it).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Both target variant-induced change in a fixed cellular context, not change caused by a protein acting in trans.

existing_models.name: m7GFinder, Deep-m7G, BERT-m7G, Moss-m7G, MCAMEF-BERT (internal m7G site predictors)
existing_models.score_and_split: Deep-m7G reports area under the curve 0.960 (full transcript) and 0.845 (mature RNA) on independent test sets, against 0.653-0.898 for earlier tools (from abstracts in search results).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Class imbalance and whether predicted sites are functional; none predicts what a given m7G site does to splicing.

backbone.name: SpliceBERT or DNABERT-2 (DNA language models; SpliceBERT is pretrained on precursor-messenger-RNA sequence and is the closer match)
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU: ~14,832 windows of ~1 kb embedded once and cached, then logistic regression or gradient boosting
backbone.licence: Weights are public on Hugging Face; I did not open the individual licence files, so exact terms are unverified

integration.partner_dataset: m7GHub V2.0 m7GDB (430,898 m7G sites across 23 species, human sites mapped to hg38; its own Nucleic Acids Research paper confirms the download)
integration.join_key: hg38 genomic coordinates (overlap of an m7G site with the event's intron or exon), plus Ensembl gene ID for the intron events
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do internal m7G sites that other labs mapped independently actually sit inside the introns NSP14 causes to be retained, or is the paper's mechanistic link between m7G and intron retention only a correlation between two separate effects of the same perturbation?

controls.positive_control: The model must recover textbook intron-retention determinants (short, GC-rich introns with weak 5' donor sites) and must predict event length from the sequence window near-perfectly.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle the UP/CTRL direction label within each event type and confirm collapse to the 60.1% majority baseline; replace windows with dinucleotide-shuffled sequence of the same length.
controls.external_validation: None truly independent: no second NSP14 dataset exists and nothing has a year or source column. The closest substitute is training on the poly(A) table and testing on the m7G-pulldown table after removing the 2,868 shared events.

honest_claim_h3: Among splicing events that already shifted by at least 15 PSI points when NSP14 was over-expressed in HEK293T cells in a single experiment, local genomic sequence predicts the direction of the shift; the data cannot support any claim about which events respond at all, because unchanged events were filtered out before deposit.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the DNA sequence around each splice site to predict which way a coronavirus enzyme shifts that exon's inclusion.
plain_idea.train_on: One row per splicing event: the genomic sequence window around the exon or intron boundaries (pulled from the human genome using the hg38 coordinates in the file), its length and event type. 6,200 events from normal messenger RNA and 8,632 from m7G-enriched messenger RNA, counted in the downloaded files.
plain_idea.predict: Whether the event goes up or down (and by how much) when the viral protein NSP14 is expressed. The true answer is the percent-spliced-in value measured from RNA-sequencing reads in three NSP14 and three control replicates, already in the table.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Coronavirus epitranscriptomics labs would learn whether the splicing damage NSP14 causes is written in the local sequence or is a general, non-sequence-specific breakdown; even a failure pins down the measurement noise floor of this kind of experiment.

more_or_better_data.why: Only 6,200 and 8,632 events from one cell line, versus SpliceAI and Pangolin trained on genome-wide splice-site usage across whole transcriptomes and four species. The one thing we have that they do not is a perturbation they never saw: a viral methyltransferase expressed in human cells.

confidence_score.why: Three replicates per condition let us estimate per-event measurement noise (I measured 7.4 and 11.5 PSI standard deviation in the NSP14 condition versus 1.5 and 2.9 in controls), which splicing predictors do not report. Three replicates is thin for calibration.

models_beatable.why: SpliceAI (2019) is old, but Pangolin (2022) and SpliceAI2 (2024) are recent and evaluated on held-out chromosomes and variant sets. For the NSP14-specific change, no model exists at all, so there is nothing to beat and no published number to aim at.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The existing models predict absolute splice-site usage, a different quantity from the NSP14-induced change, so our model does not see a superset of their inputs on the same target with the same split. The 'same quantity, same way' condition fails.

label_elsewhere.sources: VastDB (the same splicing-event catalogue used here, with PSI across many human samples) and the ENCODE/ENCORE RNA-binding-protein knockdown splicing tables, which give change-in-PSI for hundreds of perturbations in K562 and HepG2 cells. Both are known public resources; I did not download either during this evaluation. m7GHub V2.0 holds the related m7G-site label, confirmed via its Nucleic Acids Research paper.
label_elsewhere.join_key: hg38 genomic coordinates and Ensembl gene ID (VastDB event IDs are already in the file for exon events)
label_elsewhere.why: Splicing change under a perturbation is measured for many other perturbations, so a model could be pretrained or externally checked on those before being asked about NSP14, but the event definitions and cell lines differ enough that the join is real work.

risks: The same gene contributes up to 27 events (counted), so random splitting puts near-identical sequence windows from one gene on both sides.
2,868 events appear in both the poly(A) and the m7G-pulldown table, so using one as a test set for the other leaks unless those events are removed.
Event length and intron/exon type are strongly tied to the event class and to the direction of change, so a model can score well by learning event type rather than sequence.
Paralogous and repeat-containing regions share sequence across genes, so held-out genes can still be near-duplicates of training genes.
The dPSI column in the m7G-pulldown table is unsigned for 3,116 rows, which silently flips the label for a third of that file if used as deposited.
leakage_plan.split: Hold out whole chromosomes, grouped so that all events of a gene stay together. The GENE column and the COORD column (from which the chromosome is parsed) are both present in the files, verified. Remove the 2,868 shared events before any cross-table test.
checks: Shuffle the UP/CTRL label within event type and confirm the model falls to the 60.1% majority baseline.
Train on event type and length alone and report that score, so the sequence model's gain over it is explicit.
Compute nearest-neighbour sequence similarity between each test window and the training windows, and report performance as a function of it.
Recompute dPSI as mean(NSP14) minus mean(control) from the two condition-mean columns and verify it against the deposited dPSI before any training.
leakage_plan.verdict: Manageable: grouped chromosome splits and dropping the shared events handle the real risks, but the unsigned-dPSI bug must be fixed first or every number is wrong in a way nothing will crash on.

success_criteria.metric: Precision among the top 50 events predicted to gain intron retention, on held-out chromosomes, because the decision a lab makes with this is which handful of introns to test by reverse-transcription PCR. Reported alongside area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for up-versus-down direction.
success_criteria.baselines: Majority class, 60.1% CTRL in the poly(A) table (3,725 of 6,200, counted in the file). A features-only model using event type and length. Pangolin or SpliceAI baseline splice-site usage as a predictor of which events move, which is the only published model runnable here.
success_criteria.success: Area under the curve >= 0.70 for direction on held-out chromosomes with genes grouped, with the event-type-and-length-only model below 0.60, and precision in the top 50 at least double the base rate.
success_criteria.kill: Area under the curve below 0.60 on held-out chromosomes after one week, or the event-type-and-length-only model within 0.02 of the sequence model, meaning sequence adds nothing.

ambitious.why: Publishes mechanistic RNA-processing analyses; would need the sequence model plus the m7GHub overlap to show that independently mapped m7G sites really do mark the introns NSP14 retains.

realistic.why: Publishes focused reanalyses and small sequence-based predictors; a modest held-out-chromosome result plus the replicate-noise and sign-convention findings on this deposit fits its scope.

fallback.journal: bioRxiv preprint plus a GEO data-correction note to the authors
fallback.why: Even a negative model result leaves two usable facts: the deposited m7G-pulldown table has unsigned dPSI for 3,116 rows, and the NSP14-condition replicate noise is 7.4-11.5 PSI against a 15 PSI calling threshold.

pitch.headline: Two clean tables, 14,832 splicing events with per-replicate measurements, from the first experiment showing a viral enzyme writing m7G inside host messenger RNA.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: A perturbation no splicing model has seen: a coronavirus methyltransferase expressed in human cells, with percent-spliced-in values for three NSP14 and three control replicates per event. Verified by parsing both files.
pitch.the_win: Show that sequence predicts the direction of NSP14-induced change at area under the curve >= 0.70 on held-out chromosomes while event type and length alone stay under 0.60.
pitch.even_if_it_fails: You still publish two verified facts: a third of the deposited m7G-pulldown table carries unsigned change values, and the NSP14-condition replicate noise (7.4-11.5 PSI) is half the 15 PSI threshold used to call events differential.
pitch.who_wants_it: Coronavirus epitranscriptomics and m7G/METTL1 groups, including this paper's authors, who would get a ranked shortlist of introns to test and a noise floor for their next experiment.

ml_idea: From the hg38 sequence window around each splicing event (embedded once with a frozen DNA language model such as SpliceBERT or DNABERT-2), predict the direction and magnitude of the NSP14-induced change in percent spliced in, using held-out-chromosome splits with genes grouped. Secondary and arguably more valuable: join the retained-intron list to m7GHub V2.0's independently mapped internal m7G sites on hg38 coordinates and test whether m7G presence inside an intron predicts its retention, which checks the paper's mechanism without generating any new data.

effort.compute_note: Tables were timed for real (both load in under a second, under 100 MB in memory). The genome FASTA download and the embedding time are estimates: ~14,832 windows of ~1 kb at roughly 1 sequence per second on a laptop CPU, not benchmarked.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check the minimum absolute dPSI in the deposited tables. I did this: it is exactly 15.0 in both files, so unchanged events are absent and no responds-versus-does-not-respond model can be built from this deposit.

verdict_reason: Every Part A killer passes and the data is genuinely clean, open and tiny: two sub-MB tables that parse first try, with per-replicate percent-spliced-in values, hg38 coordinates and a filter that matches the paper exactly. But the deposit contains only events that already changed by at least 15 PSI points, so the negatives are gone, the mutant control condition never made it into the processed tables, and everything comes from one cell line in one lab with three replicates whose noise (7.4-11.5 PSI) is half the calling threshold. Part H scores 3/8 on that basis. The remaining question, predicting the direction of change among pre-selected events, sits next to SpliceAI, Pangolin and SpliceAI2, which are open and honestly evaluated, and a null result would be uninterpretable. Park, with a clean reopening condition: if the authors deposit the unfiltered VAST-TOOLS percent-spliced-in tables including unchanged events and the M4 mutant comparison, this becomes a real project. Meanwhile the strongest thing here is the integration play (Part G, 7/8): joining the retained-intron list to m7GHub V2.0's independently mapped m7G sites tests the paper's central mechanism with no new data, but that is a two-week analysis, not an ML project.
